types.oie_definition: A major tennis championship event held annually.
types.embedding_query_text: Sports Tournament: A major tennis championship event held annually. Also called Grand Slam, tennis championship, major tournament.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: TennisComplex
candidates.comment: A local business or sports activity location featuring multiple tennis courts and related facilities. Also called tennis center, tennis club, tennis facility. Examples: 'Indian Wells Tennis Garden', a community tennis complex, a private tennis club.

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: SportsOrganization
candidates.comment: A general category for organizations involved in sports, including teams, governing bodies, and associations. Also called athletic organization, sports body, sports group. Examples: the NBA, a local youth soccer league, the International Olympic Committee.

types.oie_definition: An instance of a sports tournament occurring at a particular time and location.
types.embedding_query_text: Tournament Event: An instance of a sports tournament occurring at a particular time and location. Also called event instance, championship occurrence, tournament edition.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: Event
candidates.comment: An Event is a Thing happening at a specific time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Also called happening, occurrence, occasion. Examples: A rock concert, a public lecture, a sports match, a community festival.

candidates.label: ConferenceEvent
candidates.comment: An event specifically organized as a conference, typically involving presentations, discussions, and networking. Also called conference, convention, symposium, summit. Examples: A tech conference, an academic symposium, a business summit, a medical convention. Distinct from Event, which is a general occurrence.

candidates.label: DeliveryEvent
candidates.comment: An event representing the delivery of an item, typically a product or package. Also called Shipping event, package delivery, consignment event. Examples: A package arriving at its destination, a food delivery being completed, a furniture delivery appointment. Distinct from Order, which is the request for items, not the delivery itself.

candidates.label: EducationEvent
candidates.comment: An EducationEvent is an Event focused on learning or instruction. Also called educational activity, learning event, training session. Examples: A university lecture, a workshop on coding, a seminar on financial literacy, a school field trip.

types.oie_definition: Monetary reward given to participants for achieving specific results in a competition.
types.embedding_query_text: Prize Money: Monetary reward given to participants for achieving specific results in a competition. Also called contest prize, tournament winnings, competition reward.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: MonetaryAmount captures specific currency values like prize money amounts.

candidates.label: MonetaryGrant
candidates.comment: An intangible grant that provides a sum of money. Also called financial grant, money award, cash donation. Examples: a research grant, a scholarship, a government subsidy. Distinct from Grant, which can be non-monetary.

candidates.label: SportsEvent
candidates.comment: An event involving athletic competition or display. Also called athletic contest, game, match, sporting competition. Examples: a football game, an Olympic event, a marathon race, a tennis tournament.

candidates.label: WinAction
candidates.comment: The act of achieving victory or success in a competitive activity. Also called triumph, succeed, prevail. Examples: winning a race, winning a championship, winning an argument.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmount
candidates.comment: A structured value representing a monetary value or range, typically expressed with a currency. Also called amount of money, financial value, currency amount. Examples: "$50 USD", "£1,000 to £1,000,000 GBP", "€25.99". Distinct from PriceSpecification, which describes the price of an offer.

candidates.label: Game
candidates.comment: A Game is a CreativeWork representing a rule-governed recreational activity, often involving players assuming roles in a fictional setting. Also called pastime, play, recreational activity. Examples: A board game like Chess, a video game like Minecraft, a role-playing game like Dungeons & Dragons, a card game like Poker.

types.oie_definition: A period of 365 days as a unit of time, typically referenced by its four-digit numerical designation.
types.embedding_query_text: Year: A period of 365 days as a unit of time, typically referenced by its four-digit numerical designation. Also called calendar year, annum, yearly period.

chosen_type.label: Year
chosen_type.definition: A four-digit numerical designation representing a calendar year.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type precisely represents a calendar year as a four-digit value.

candidates.label: Duration
candidates.comment: As a Quantity, Duration represents a period of time, typically expressed in ISO 8601 format. Also called time span, period, length of time. Examples: "PT1H30M" (1 hour 30 minutes), "P3D" (3 days), "PT2H" (2 hours).

candidates.label: Date
candidates.comment: Date is a data type representing a specific calendar date, typically formatted according to ISO 8601. Also called calendar date, specific day. Examples: "2023-10-27", "1999-12-31", "0001-01-01".

candidates.label: Schedule
candidates.comment: A definition of a repeating time period used to describe a regularly occurring event, specifying frequency, days, and start/end times. Also called timetable, recurring event plan, calendar entry, routine. Examples: a weekly yoga class schedule, a bus route timetable, a daily meeting schedule, a concert series calendar.

candidates.label: DayOfWeek
candidates.comment: An enumeration representing a specific day of the week, used for scheduling or recurring events. Also called Weekday, calendar day, day name. Examples: Monday, Tuesday, Saturday, Sunday. Distinct from Date, which specifies a particular calendar date.

candidates.label: Season
candidates.comment: A distinct period within a media series, such as a television show, radio program, or video game. Also called media season, series installment, broadcast season. Examples: 'Season 1 of Game of Thrones', 'The Fall 2023 radio season', 'Chapter 3 of a video game series'. Distinct from TVSeason, which is specifically for television broadcasts.

types.oie_definition: An individual who competes in sports at a professional level.
types.embedding_query_text: Athlete: An individual who competes in sports at a professional level. Also called sports competitor, player, competitor.

chosen_type.label: Person
chosen_type.justification: Person is the appropriate base type for individual human competitors.

candidates.label: SportsActivityLocation
candidates.comment: A local business or facility providing a venue for sports activities. Also called sports venue, athletic facility, recreation center, playing field. Examples: a local gym, a public tennis court, a community swimming pool, a golf course.

candidates.label: Person
candidates.comment: A Person is an individual human being, whether alive, dead, undead, or fictional. Also called individual, human, character. Examples: John Doe, Albert Einstein, Sherlock Holmes. Distinct from Organization, which is a group of people.

types.oie_definition: A specific geographical place where an event occurs.
types.embedding_query_text: Location: A specific geographical place where an event occurs. Also called venue, site, location.

chosen_type.label: Place
chosen_type.justification: Place represents a specific geographical location for events like Flushing Meadows.

candidates.label: Place
candidates.comment: A Place is an entity that has a somewhat fixed, physical extension. Also called location, venue, site. Examples: a city, a building, a park, a specific address. Distinct from Event, which is a happening in time.

candidates.label: TouristAttraction
candidates.comment: A specific place or feature that draws tourists due to its interest or appeal. Also called point of interest, visitor attraction, landmark. Examples: the Eiffel Tower, a national park, a historical museum, a famous statue. Distinct from TouristDestination, which is a broader area containing one or more attractions.

types.oie_definition: The aggregate monetary reward distributed across all categories of a competition.
types.embedding_query_text: Total Prize Money: The aggregate monetary reward distributed across all categories of a competition. Also called total tournament prize, overall competition payout, combined award pool.

chosen_type.label: MonetaryAmount
chosen_type.justification: MonetaryAmount represents the total aggregate prize money as a specific currency value.

candidates.label: MonetaryAmountDistribution
candidates.comment: A quantitative value distribution representing a statistical distribution of monetary amounts. Also called money distribution, financial range, income distribution. Examples: "average salary range", "distribution of asset values", "price range for a product category".

candidates.label: AggregateRating
candidates.comment: An AggregateRating is a Rating that represents the average or summary of multiple individual ratings or reviews. Also called average rating, collective rating, summary score, overall rating. Examples: A product's 4.5-star rating based on 100 reviews, a movie's Rotten Tomatoes score, a restaurant's Yelp rating. Distinct from Rating, which is a single individual rating.

types.oie_definition: A specific round or phase in a sports competition where players advance through the tournament.
types.embedding_query_text: Competition Stage: A specific round or phase in a sports competition where players advance through the tournament. Also called match stage, tournament round, competition round.

chosen_type.label: CompetitionStage
chosen_type.definition: A round or phase in a sports competition denoting progression through the tournament.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type captures specific tournament stages like quarter-finals or winners' positions.

candidates.label: TieAction

candidates.label: SportsTeam
candidates.comment: An organization consisting of a group of athletes who compete together in a sport. Also called athletic team, squad, club, side. Examples: the Los Angeles Lakers, the New England Patriots, a high school basketball team.

candidates.label: LoseAction

Examples: losing a game, being defeated in an election, failing a competition. Distinct from AchieveAction, which is a broader category for actions that result in an outcome.

types.oie_definition: A classification within a sports competition that differentiates types of events or participant groups.
types.embedding_query_text: Competition Category: A classification within a sports competition that differentiates types of events or participant groups. Also called event category, tournament division, competition type.

chosen_type.label: CompetitionCategory
chosen_type.definition: A classification within a sports competition distinguishing participant groups or event types.
chosen_type.justification: No existing Schema.org type represents categories like wheelchair or doubles in tennis tournaments.
